## API and process contracts

The Web Application calls the Backend API through HTTPS REST/JSON. The Backend API is the identity, authorization, evidence, validation, publication, and export boundary. The Background Worker owns deterministic daily processing. The Scheduler and Replay Runner owns time, replay, acceptance, and parity work. The Agent Runtime owns bounded graph execution and agent-owned job state.

All report, interactive, and document-analysis Agent Jobs use one durable PostgreSQL queue. The Backend producer commits an idempotent job with pinned actor, scope, policy, and input references before sending an optional authenticated wake-up containing only the job ID. The Agent Runtime Runner claims and leases the canonical job from PostgreSQL, executes it, and persists its outcome. A missed wake-up cannot lose work; polling and lease recovery remain authoritative. The Backend validates persisted outcomes and exposes authorized job status/results to the Web Application. The Agent Runtime Gateway produces interactive jobs; the Document Processing Runner produces document jobs only after a successful parse; an edit revision is created by the producer for that workload type.

The main nightly path is:

```text
Scheduler and Replay Runner
  -> Backend Run Coordinator
  -> PostgreSQL job plan
  -> Background Worker stages
  -> manager-scoped Evidence Package and Canonical Report JSON
  -> PostgreSQL unlocks the pinned Agent Job
  -> Agent Runtime Runner claims, executes, and persists outcome
  -> deterministic validation
  -> independent publication
```

# Data and processing

## Daily data plane

The daily data path is deterministic. It uses this sequence:

```text
Source Intake
  -> Schema Registry
  -> Normalizer
  -> Data Quality
  -> Deduplication and Conflict Handling
  -> Canonical Storage
  -> Daily Snapshot
  -> KPI Engine
  -> Signal and Workflow Engine
  -> Evidence and Agent
  -> Validator and Publisher
```

The system reads input only from `DATA_DIR`. It writes delivery output only to `OUTPUT_DIR`. It processes drops from `day_000` through `day_090` in order.

A report for the morning of business day D can use valid data and manager input through the end of day D-1. Data that arrives during a run does not change that run. Each run pins the data, organization, policy, and configuration versions.

Each source has a versioned schema contract. The contract defines required columns, canonical names, aliases, types, formats, units, null rules, allowed values, primary keys, and error behavior. Unknown structures are not guessed.

Raw source data and canonical data remain separate. Each canonical record keeps a link to its source file, drop, and hash. Invalid or conflicting records are quarantined and do not enter a valid snapshot.

Missing data does not stop all publication. A dependent KPI is `null`. The system records the condition as a data issue. A data issue is not a business signal.

Late or corrected data causes a complete rebuild in the first version. A rebuild creates a new restated report version. It does not overwrite the original published report.

PostgreSQL 18 is the only product database and the product calculation engine. It stores canonical data, snapshots, KPI results, workflow and signal state, durable jobs, receipts, reports, and audit records. Normal .NET transactions use EF Core and Npgsql. Job claims and approved KPI SQL can use Npgsql directly.

## Normalization boundary

Source Intake verifies the manifest and source hash. Schema Registry selects the versioned source contract. Normalizer converts accepted source fields to canonical names, types, formats, units, and timezone rules. Data Quality and Deduplication and Conflict Handling run after normalization and before a record enters canonical storage.

The pipeline does not infer an unknown schema, unit, key, or alias. A failed source record remains outside the valid snapshot and has a traceable issue receipt.

## KPI acceptance plane

KPI acceptance is separate from the daily product path:

```text
Read-only reference SQL
  -> SQLite inside Acceptance Test Harness
  -> reference result

Equivalent pinned snapshot
  -> translated PostgreSQL SQL
  -> product result

Reference result + product result
  -> Acceptance Test Harness (parity check)
  -> Parity Receipt
```

SQLite is embedded only in the Acceptance Test Harness. It is not a product database, product container, or daily runtime dependency. The reference SQL and KPI Dictionary remain read-only.

The parity check inside the Acceptance Test Harness compares row sets, nulls, values, median translation, time intervals, decimal division, timezone behavior, and date boundaries. The maximum accepted evaluation tolerance is one percent. A PostgreSQL translation is not accepted until its parity evidence passes. Parity is one acceptance check, not a separate product component; the former KPI Parity Validator is folded into the harness (ADR-0016 amended, doc 16 §6.3).

Agent Runtime has no role in SQL translation, KPI calculation, or parity repair.

# Security and trust

The following inputs are untrusted:

- Source files
- Ticket text
- Manager uploads
- User prompts
- Language-model output

Untrusted input cannot change policy, credentials, report destinations, approved numbers, or the tool allowlist.

The Backend API creates a trusted identity context. The Authorization Service derives the permitted resource, column, purpose, predicate, and organization scope. Authorization is applied before evidence reaches the language model. Output validation applies the scope again before delivery or publication.

## Business-data query path

The Agent Runtime requests business evidence from the Backend API Evidence Service. The Evidence Service sends approved query requests to the Query Gateway. The Query Gateway validates and executes the registered read-only operation. It returns only evidence that is inside the trusted actor, purpose, policy, snapshot, row, and column scope.

Ad-hoc Text-to-SQL questions use the same path with an added generation contract (ADR-0023). Scope is pinned before the model writes SQL. The model may name only approved semantic views and KPI definitions, never raw business tables, and has no database credential. The Backend injects the scope predicate so generated SQL cannot omit it. After validation the query is persisted with a new `query_id`, scope, and result hash and shown beside the answer. "Registered" for an ad-hoc query means persisted, validated, and auditable; it does not mean pre-approved in the KPI Dictionary. A number in the answer must map to a `value` and `query_id` pair. `refused_out_of_scope` is used when data exists outside the manager's subset; `data_unavailable` is used when the data is not in the system sources.

The query path uses defense in depth:

- Registered read-only queries
- Relation allowlists
- Column projections
- SQL AST validation
- Purpose checks
- PostgreSQL row-level security
- `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`
- Non-owner runtime roles
- No `SUPERUSER` or `BYPASSRLS` role in runtime paths
- Scope-aware caching
- Query and access audit records
- Negative leakage tests for each manager role

The language model has no database credential. It has no direct file credential. The Model Gateway is the only external model path. It applies the approved token, time, retry, and cost controls.

## Agent Runtime database boundary

ADR-0019 permits a restricted Agent Runtime PostgreSQL role. The final role name is open. Migration from the existing `agent_query_reader` role, or continued use of that role, is also open.

The restricted role can access only job-scoped agent state:

| Allowed state | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Agent Job | Claim and inspect the assigned durable job |
| Lease and Attempt | Control concurrent execution and recovery |
| Dependency state | Confirm that the claimed job is ready |
| LangGraph checkpoint | Resume bounded graph execution |
| Conversation state | Read and write manager-scoped bounded history |
| Candidate and failure state | Persist the runtime outcome |
| Job-scoped Evidence view | Reload references already approved for the job |

Direct access to these data areas is forbidden:

- Orders and operational facts
- Customers and customer identifiers
- Organization and authorization policy tables
- KPI facts and unrestricted report data
- Database migration metadata
- Row-level security policy administration

The Agent Runtime does not perform migrations, grant permissions, change policies, or execute arbitrary business SQL.

## Other trust boundaries

- Protected uploads are treated as data, not instructions.
- The Document Processing Runner parses only archived bytes with an approved contract (the former Document Parser is a function inside it).
- Output Validator verifies schema, scope, and evidence before publication or export.
- Submission Exporter writes only validated contract fields to a contained path below `OUTPUT_DIR`.
- OpenTelemetry and Langfuse instrumentation must remove secrets, raw restricted business data, full documents, and unauthorized manager context.

A minimal access projection matrix is required before authorization and scoped-query implementation. It must cover Senior Manager, Unit Manager, and Team Supervisor and specify Resource, Row scope, Allowed columns, Purpose, and individual-data access. This document does not define the matrix entries and does not approve a new database-role name or a wider data projection.

# Runtime flows

## Agent Job lifecycle and persistence

PostgreSQL is the authoritative job and state store for all report, interactive, and document-analysis Agent Jobs. A job is committed before any wake-up and carries an idempotency key plus pinned actor, policy, scope, and workload-specific input references. The Agent Runtime Runner claims a Ready job under a lease and records attempts and terminal state. A wake-up may reduce latency, but polling and lease recovery prevent work from being lost. Runtime outcome persistence and deterministic validation are separate states; the UI or publisher consumes only the validated result.

## Nightly report flow

The Replay Command selects a business day, derives the pinned business date and cutoff, and loads acceptance limits and run options. In the implementation model, the former Simulation Clock and Evaluation Profile Loader are functions inside the Replay Command (doc 16 §6.1).

The Run Status Client asks the Backend Run Coordinator to create a pinned run and its complete job plan. PostgreSQL stores job dependencies, manager order, and durable job state.

The Background Worker claims ready deterministic jobs. It runs ingestion, snapshot, KPI, workflow, signal, and report-evidence stages. A Report Evidence Job creates one manager-scoped Evidence Package and Canonical Report JSON, then unlocks its preplanned Agent Job.

One PostgreSQL-backed Agent Job Runner in Agent Runtime claims and leases every Ready report, interactive, or document-analysis Agent Job. It reloads the pinned actor, scope, policy, and workload-specific inputs from PostgreSQL, runs the bounded graph, persists the candidate or explicit failure, and only then submits the outcome for deterministic validation. The bounded agent cannot change canonical numbers or widen scope.

Backend producers commit an idempotent job before optionally sending an authenticated wake-up containing only the job ID. The wake-up is a latency hint, not a payload or source of truth. Runtime polling and lease recovery find jobs even when a wake-up is lost. The Web Application receives the job ID and polls the authorized Backend status API; queued/running work remains pending, and only a persisted validated result is presented as ready for review or delivery.

The Output Validator checks schema, evidence, scope, report rules, and model failure state. The Publisher publishes valid manager reports independently. A required manager failure makes the day `incomplete`, but it does not remove valid reports for other managers.

## Validation and submission export flow

Output Validator checks the candidate against the read-only reference schema. It also checks actor scope, evidence references, path containment, and output rules. It records a Validation Receipt with `trace_id`.

Publisher records the valid product result in PostgreSQL. Submission Exporter reads only a validated final result. It directly joins `OUTPUT_DIR` with `briefs/day_XXX/<manager_id>.json` or `qa/<question_id>.json`. It resolves the path, verifies containment, rejects absolute paths and `..`, writes a temporary file on the same filesystem, flushes and closes it, and performs an atomic rename. It records the content hash, relative path, `trace_id`, and Export Receipt.

For `OUTPUT_DIR=/submission`, the exporter writes directly below `/submission`. It does not create `/submission/submission`.

The complete Decision Effect remains an internal versioned PostgreSQL record. Export uses only fields and values that the reference output schema permits.

## Interactive question and manager decision flow

The Web Application sends an authenticated request to the Backend API. The fixed handler is selected by in-process dispatch (the former Manager Request Router is a function, doc 16 §6.2) and the Authorization Service pins the permitted scope. The Agent Runtime Gateway commits an idempotent interactive Agent Job to PostgreSQL with actor, policy, scope, request, and conversation references. It returns the committed job ID to the request handler, which returns it to the UI; the Gateway may also send the Agent Runtime an authenticated wake-up containing only the job ID.

The Agent Runtime Runner claims and leases the job from PostgreSQL, reloads its canonical inputs and pinned scope, and invokes the bounded graph. Conversation and evidence tools use their explicitly authorized Backend services. The Runner persists its candidate or explicit execution failure before submitting the outcome to Output Validator. The validator persists its receipt and transitions the job to validated or rejected. The UI polls the Backend status API, which returns only the owning manager's authorized status and validated result reference. Editing an interactive decision card creates a new idempotent revision job through the Agent Runtime Gateway; confirm, edit, or reject remains a human command, and only a confirmed card enters Decision and Follow-Up.

## Document decision flow

The Document Processing Runner archives the original upload and runs deterministic parsing internally (the former Document Parser is a function inside it, doc 16 §6.1). On unsupported or invalid content, parsing returns an explicit failure and no Agent Job is created. On successful parsing, immutable fragments and a parse receipt are stored, then the Document Processing Runner commits one durable document-analysis Agent Job with pinned actor, scope, policy, and fragment references. It returns the job ID to the request handler and may request a best-effort job-ID-only wake-up through the Gateway; the Runtime Runner still claims canonical job data from PostgreSQL. The same Agent Runtime Runner claims and leases the job, executes the bounded document graph, and persists its candidate or execution failure before validation. The UI polls authorized job status. Decision and Follow-Up presents only a valid card for manager review. A manager edit creates a revision through the Document Processing Runner using the approved fragments; only a confirmed card can enter the decision record.

## Replay and evaluation

Replay runs days in order and resumes from the last terminal day. The Acceptance Test Harness runs replay, SQLite-to-PostgreSQL KPI parity, hidden-data, regression, leakage, performance, cost, and output-contract checks outside the daily publication path.

## Trace correlation

REST calls propagate W3C `traceparent`. Durable jobs persist trace context or use a Span Link when asynchronous processing starts. Run, Job, Validation Receipt, Publication Receipt, Parity Receipt, and Export Receipt records include `trace_id`. Telemetry export is optional and fail-open. It does not replace PostgreSQL job state or receipts.

# Deployment and operations

## Runtime services and deployment profiles

DIDRAH has two deployment profiles over the same logical containers and processes. Docker Compose is the local development and UI demonstration profile. A single image with one batch entrypoint is the graded evaluation profile (ADR-0021). The professor runs only the evaluation profile.

The approved runtime has separate processes and containers:

1. **web** serves the React, TypeScript, and Vite application.
2. **backend-api** runs ASP.NET Core on .NET 10 LTS.
3. **background-worker** runs the .NET 10 Worker Service.
4. **scheduler-replay** runs a .NET 10 console or Worker Service process.
5. **agent-runtime** runs Python 3.12, LangGraph, and Pydantic.
6. **postgresql** runs PostgreSQL 18.

The Scheduler implementation remains open between a console process and a Worker Service. The selected implementation must keep a separate Scheduler process and container.

Docker Compose does not add a message broker, distributed cache, service mesh, or new microservice. Kubernetes is outside the approved scope.

## Evaluation profile: one image, one command

The graded evaluation uses one image and one non-interactive `docker run` (ADR-0021). This supersedes Compose only for evaluation packaging. The logical C4 containers are unchanged and run as separate processes inside the image, with their own database roles and contracts. The Web Application is served only by the Compose development profile; the evaluator reads contract JSON from `OUTPUT_DIR` and does not use the web interfaces.

All dependencies are installed at image build time. Nothing is installed at run time. The entrypoint reads `DATA_DIR` and `OUTPUT_DIR` from environment variables, processes drops from `day_000` through `day_090` in order, applies scripted manager input on its own day, produces the morning reports for days 62 through 91, exports them below `OUTPUT_DIR`, and exits with code zero. The PostgreSQL data directory is created fresh inside the container at run time and is not baked into the image, so both evaluator runs start from identical state.

The command given to the professor is:

```powershell
docker build -t team_x .

docker run --rm `
  --cpus=4 --memory=16g `
  -v /eval/holdout/arka_dataset:/data:ro `
  -v /eval/results/team_x:/submission `
  -e LLM_API_KEY=*** -e LLM_BASE_URL=... -e LLM_MODEL=deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 `
  -e DATA_DIR=/data -e OUTPUT_DIR=/submission `
  team_x
```

## LLM configuration

The evaluation profile uses `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` (ADR-0022). The three variables `LLM_API_KEY`, `LLM_BASE_URL`, and `LLM_MODEL` are injected at run time and declared by name in `.env.example`. No key is stored in the project or repository. `temperature` is zero. Each model call has a hard 30-second timeout and at most two retries with bounded backoff. A model failure removes only LLM narrative and leaves deterministic canonical JSON valid. Other generation parameters remain implementation configuration.

## Network and security boundaries

Web can call only the Backend API. Web has no direct database connection. PostgreSQL and Protected File Archive are not public services. API, Worker, Scheduler, and Agent Runtime use only their required PostgreSQL permissions. Agent Runtime permissions follow ADR-0019.

## Volumes and filesystem boundaries

Compose mounts or defines:

- Read-only `DATA_DIR`
- Writable `OUTPUT_DIR`
- Protected File Archive volume
- PostgreSQL 18 data volume
- Service-specific configuration and secrets

Input data remains read-only. Submission Exporter is the only writer of contract output. It resolves and contains every target path below `OUTPUT_DIR` before an atomic write.

## Optional observability profile

The optional observability profile adds `otel-collector` as an infrastructure container. Product services send OTLP to the collector when the profile is active. The collector exports permitted agent and model telemetry to Langfuse.

Langfuse is external unless a later decision approves self-hosting. The managed or self-hosted choice remains open. OTLP/gRPC or OTLP/HTTP for backend services is a configuration decision.

Observability is fail-open. Product services continue their core work when the collector or Langfuse is unavailable. Collector queues and retries do not replace PostgreSQL durable jobs. No additional observability backend is in scope.

## Evaluation operating constraints

- Four CPU cores
- Sixteen GB RAM
- No GPU
- Network access only to the configured LLM API
- Read-only `/data`
- Writable `/submission`
- One-command non-interactive `docker run` execution
- Dependencies installed during image build
- UTF-8 input and output
- Business timezone `Asia/Tehran`

## Operations

The system records stage duration, accepted and rejected rows, query results, KPI counts, signal changes, report results, model tokens, model cost, retries, access denials, result hashes, and artifact versions. W3C `traceparent` is propagated across REST calls. Asynchronous jobs persist trace context or use Span Links. Receipts store `trace_id` for correlation.

Failed jobs record an explicit terminal failure when the approved policy requires it. Model-call timeout, retry, and no-narrative fallback follow ADR-0022. Agent Job deadline, dead-letter policy, and reconciliation cadence remain open implementation decisions.

ADR-0011 is accepted for the Evaluation profile. Evidence required for replay and the two-run check remains available for the duration of an evaluation run. Production retention periods, backup frequency, RPO, RTO, audit access, and the restore procedure remain open.

# Quality attributes

## Correctness

Published numbers come from registered deterministic queries. The system stores the SQL, result, snapshot, scope, and `query_id` for each published number. The UI, serializer, and language model do not recalculate or round a KPI.

The parity check inside the Acceptance Test Harness compares PostgreSQL results with the SQLite reference oracle. It checks row sets, nulls, values, translation semantics, timezone behavior, and date boundaries. A translation needs a Parity Receipt before acceptance. Parity is owned by the harness, not a separate component (ADR-0016 amended).

## Security

The system must prevent data leakage across the Senior Manager, Unit Manager, and Team Supervisor scopes. Authorization is applied before model use and after model output.

Leakage tests must cover row, column, resource, purpose, organization, conversation, and job scope. Tests must also prove that the restricted Agent Runtime role cannot read business tables or change database policy.

## Reproducibility

Each run uses pinned inputs and an injected business clock. An identical run must produce identical numbers and signals. Published reports are immutable.

Replay must preserve source hashes, schema versions, snapshots, configuration, query identifiers, receipts, and published report versions.

## Resilience

A missing source can reduce data completeness without stopping all publication. A model-provider failure must not stop deterministic calculation or valid canonical JSON. A manager-specific failure must not remove other valid manager reports.

A lost Agent Runtime wake-up must not lose a committed job. Collector or Langfuse failure must not stop core workflows.

## Performance and cost

The evaluation requirement is at most five minutes for each processing day and at most five US dollars for the complete 30-day run (not per day). The model is selected in ADR-0022 (`deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`). The model call timeout is a hard 30-second limit with at most two bounded-backoff retries; on exhaustion the report is emitted with correct numbers and no LLM narrative. Two runs of the container must produce identical numbers and signals (ADR-0026). Internal budget allocation and Agent Job deadline remain open.

The Acceptance Test Harness measures replay duration, manager-output coverage, model usage, and total cost without changing the daily product path.

## Maintainability

A new source, KPI, organization node, or manager level should use a versioned adapter, registry entry, or configuration change. It should not require a pipeline redesign.

## Auditability

Every published result must link to its evidence, query, snapshot, configuration, policy scope, validation result, and publication receipt.

Run, Job, Validation Receipt, Publication Receipt, Parity Receipt, and Export Receipt records include `trace_id` correlation metadata.

## Observability

OpenTelemetry is the common instrumentation and trace-correlation standard. REST calls propagate W3C `traceparent`. Asynchronous jobs use persisted trace context or a Span Link.

Langfuse is limited to permitted agent traces, model calls, token usage, cost, agent evaluation, and permitted prompt or model metadata. Telemetry must exclude secrets, raw restricted business data, full documents, and unauthorized manager context. Telemetry export is optional and fail-open. In the graded Evaluation profile the outbound network is closed except the LLM API, so Langfuse/OTLP export is disabled (ADR-0027); it remains available only in the development profile.

PostgreSQL stores correlation metadata and architecture receipts. It does not store full spans, traces, or general telemetry logs.

## Acceptance coverage

The Acceptance Test Harness covers:

- Ordered replay, restart behavior, and an organization change during replay without a code change.
- SQLite-to-PostgreSQL KPI parity, zero incorrect published numbers, hidden-data tests, and regression tests.
- Ten morning reports before 07:30, with no more than five items in each report.
- At least 90% of required signals detected within 24 hours, with the correct owner and cause.
- All three workflows reconstructed with SLA and bottleneck results.
- At least 85% acceptance accuracy for scoped manager questions.
- Zero cross-scope leakage and explicit prompt-injection tests for ticket, file, and upload text.
- Fairness checks that prevent unsupported individual blame and restrict individual data to an approved direct-supervisor workload purpose.
- Q03 checks for the `U_SAL` monthly target, net revenue through yesterday, and proportional target attainment.
- Output-contract validation, path containment, atomic export, and trace correlation.
- At most five minutes per processing day and at most five US dollars for the complete 30-day run.
- Equal numbers and discovered signals in two runs with the same inputs.

# 15. Implementation Contract (authoritative TA clarifications)

This document is the single implementation-ready contract derived from the instructor Q&A in `ta.txt`. Where an older brief statement disagrees with this document, **this document wins**. It closes `ISSUE-V3-02`, `DOC-GAP-V3-04`, and `ISSUE-V3-09` for the Evaluation profile. `ISSUE-V3-01` remains open only for the access projection matrix entries required by `04-security-and-trust.md`.

Status: **Accepted for implementation**. Every rule below is testable by the Acceptance Test Harness.

## 1. KPI numbers and SQL parity

- The reference number of every KPI is produced by executing the metric-dictionary SQL on **SQLite**. A different engine is allowed only if results are identical.
- SQLite `median()` is equivalent to PostgreSQL `percentile_cont(0.5)`, **not** `percentile_disc`.
- `julianday(b) - julianday(a)` is in **days**; PostgreSQL `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM b - a)` returns seconds and must be converted explicitly to the KPI unit (hours or days).
- Percentages use `100.0 *` to avoid integer division.
- Rounding, date types, and timezone (`Asia/Tehran`) can move a record to another day. Per-KPI rounding follows the KPI dictionary.
- Compare output with the reference SQL on the dev dataset. **±1% is the accepted KPI-parity/evaluation tolerance.** The brief's "zero tolerance" applies only to matching a number in the report text to a `value`/`query_id` pair in JSON, not to KPI computation.
- A Parity Receipt is required before a translated KPI is accepted.

## 2. Reference machine, network, and determinism

| Item | Required value |
|---|---|
| CPU | 4 cores |
| RAM | 16 GB |
| GPU | None |
| Network | **Only the LLM API**; all other internet egress is closed |
| Data mount | `/data` read-only |
| Time budget | **At most 5 minutes per processing day** |
| Dependencies | All installed at image build time; no install at run time |
| Local LLM | Not permitted (no GPU, would exceed the time budget) |
| Model calls | Retry with bounded backoff and a finite timeout; on failure emit the report with correct numbers and no LLM narrative |
| Temperature | `0` for stable text |
| Repeated runs | The container is executed **twice**; numbers and discovered signals must be identical across runs |

Determinism rules: no host clock in product time, no unordered iteration affecting output, no random sampling, pinned input hashes and configuration, stable sort keys, and LLM text never used as a source of numbers or signal status.

## 3. LLM provider, cost, and secrets

- Provider is free as long as it is reachable through an API. The model and version are declared in ADR-0022.
- **The $5 ceiling covers the entire 30-day replay run, not a single day.**
- Cost = logged input tokens + logged output tokens × the provider's official rate on the evaluation day. Every call logs provider, model, token counts, latency, status, and trace context. The computed total is reconciled with the provider dashboard.
- No API key in the project or repository. Only `.env.example` with `LLM_API_KEY`, `LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_MODEL`. The key is injected as an environment variable, delivered to the instructor over a private channel, and revoked after Demo Day.
- Langfuse/OTLP export is disabled in the graded Evaluation profile because outbound network is closed. Telemetry is optional and fail-open.

## 4. Docker entrypoint and paths

- `/data`: hidden data with the same structure as `arka_dataset`, read-only.
- `/submission`: writable; contains `briefs/day_XXX/<manager_id>.json` and `qa/<question_id>.json`.
- One command performs the whole run: process drops night-by-night from `day_000` through `day_090`, apply `manager_inputs` on their own day, and produce reports for mornings `day_062` through `day_091`. No manual or interactive step.
- Read paths from `DATA_DIR` and `OUTPUT_DIR` environment variables; never hardcode them.
- Exit code must be zero on success. The internal database, logs, and dashboard remain inside the container; nothing is written outside `OUTPUT_DIR`.

## 5. Data issues

`data_issues` entries carry `type` and `source` with these exact literal values:

| Situation | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| File missing on first morning | One `data_issues` entry with `type: "missing"`; dependent KPIs are `null`, never `0` |
| File still missing | Repeat `missing` every morning until arrival; never in `items`; no penalty for repetition |
| File arrives | On the next morning, exactly one entry with `type: "late_arrival"`; recompute that day's KPIs; if recomputation creates a signal, include it in that same morning's report |
| Duplicate export row | Deduplicate first; same morning `data_issues` with `source: "orders"`, `type: "duplicate"`; the apparent order-count/revenue jump must not become an `item` |

Canonical deduplication keys: `order_id`, `ticket_id`, `lead_id`, `task_id`. Event tables use the composite key `(entity_id, event_type, event_time)`. Duplicate rows are byte-identical.

A data issue is not a business signal. The only exception is a genuine KPI signal created by recomputation after a late arrival, which is published that same morning.

## 6. Lead lifecycle and KPI populations

- A lead with no progress after first contact is **abandoned**, not a bottleneck. CRM records no "rejection" event.
- `K_WF3_SLA_7D` and `K_ENT_WINRATE_30D` count only **closed** leads (won or lost).
- `K_ENT_PIPELINE` counts only opportunities for which a proposal was sent.
- Adopted rule: no progress after **14 days** = abandoned.
- The absence of a rejection event is reported once as a data-quality note, not as a daily signal.

## 7. Signal lifecycle and direction

- Signal types: target deviation, abnormal trend, sudden change, workflow slowdown, backlog, monthly-target risk.
- Importance criteria: deviation size, customer impact, financial impact, cross-unit effect, statistical confidence, manager-declared priority.
- Every signal has one owner, assigned to the lowest level able to resolve it. At most five items per manager report.
- `dow_baseline`: only deviation in the **unfavorable** direction is a signal. The KPI dictionary `direction` column defines favorable direction: `1` = more is better, `-1` = less is better. `K_SUP_TICKETS` has `direction = -1`: a decrease is not a signal; an increase beyond N% is. A large favorable deviation is not an alert and may be shown outside `items`.
- Rule R5, exact text: «انحراف بیش از N٪ در جهت نامطلوب (طبق direction) سیگنال است.»
- A KPI that crosses `crit` on its first day is `new` for the owner and `escalated` for the higher manager the same morning. If it passes `warn` first and then `crit`: day one is `new`, then `ongoing` with escalation history; on the day it becomes `crit`, or when time above `warn` exceeds `escalate_after_days`, it is `escalated`.
- A workflow KPI or organization-level KPI crossing `warn` is also `escalated` for the Senior Manager. Co-cause signals are aggregated into one Senior Manager item.
- A signal without meaningful change must not reappear as `new`; repetition is penalized. Escalation is allowed only with explicit history and reason.
- Escalation defaults live in the KPI dictionary and are editable: team supervisor 2 days, unit manager 3 days.

## 10. Decision effect and success metrics

- Measure effect with the decision's own success metric, but account for concurrent factors. A simple before/after comparison is insufficient when a campaign coincided. Use either workload normalization (e.g. orders per picking staff) or comparison with a similar case without the decision.
- Every effect result states: whether the success metric was met; the effect estimate with method and assumptions; confidence level and confounding factors. If data cannot separate the effect, say «اثر قابل جدا کردن نیست» — not "no effect".
- The system proposes a success metric on the decision card; the manager confirms it at decision time. "10% improvement" is only a fallback default when no better metric exists.
- Success metric components: target KPI and target value (preferably return below the `warn` threshold or reach the dictionary `target`, not an arbitrary percentage); measurement window (3–5 days); guardrail KPI with its limit.
- Track both target and guardrail on following days. `decision_followups` reports effect direction as `improved`, `worsened`, `no_change`, or `too_early`. A guardrail breach is itself a business signal.

## 12. Design quality bar

Backend API, Background Worker, and Agent Runtime follow the scoping rule in `16-domain-model.md`, section **Scoping rule (read first)**. Full tactical DDD applies only to an atomic, acceptance-tested invariant that is mutated from more than one place. Other concepts remain entities, value objects, commands, derived read models, append-only records, or functions inside an owning component. This contract does not require a new component, service, broker, or deployment boundary. Performance budget, determinism, row-level security, and fail-open behavior are acceptance gates, not tuning items.

# 16. Domain Model (scoped DDD) for the runtime components

This document defines the tactical Domain-Driven Design model for the three runtime components that carry business complexity: **Backend API**, **Background Worker**, and **Agent Runtime**. It is the implementation contract for module boundaries, aggregate invariants, ports, and domain events. It complements the C4 component inventory in docs 10, 11, and 13; where a C4 component name appears below, it is the adapter or application service implementing the named domain role.

Status: **Accepted for implementation**.

> **Implementation source note.** This document and docs 10–13 define the component and domain boundaries used for implementation. The DSL is a visual overview of these documents. It does not define a separate implementation model.

## 0. Scoping rule (read first)

Full tactical DDD is expensive. Apply it **only where an invariant is atomic, acceptance-tested, and mutated from more than one place**. Use this test:

> If you cannot complete the sentence "this must never happen, even under concurrency," the concept is not an aggregate. It is an entity inside an aggregate, a value object, a derived read model, or an append-only record.

Consequences of the rule:

- **Aggregate** → keep a root, invariants, a repository port, and domain events.
- **Entity inside an aggregate** → keep as a child of the owning root; no separate repository or component.
- **Value object / command / DTO** → keep as an immutable type; no lifecycle, no component.
- **Derived read model** → rebuild from the source of truth; no invariant, no component.
- **Append-only record** → a repository adapter writes it; it is not a domain aggregate or a component.
- **Stateless rule or parser** → a function or module inside the owning component; no ports, no events, no view node.

A component earns its own box only if it coordinates at least one invariant-bearing entity set. This rule drives every merge and elimination in §6.

## 0.1 Shared rules

- **Modular monolith, not distributed microservices.** Bounded contexts are enforced by module boundaries and explicit application-service APIs, not by network calls. Cross-context calls go through an Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) that translates foreign models.
- **Layering inside each context:** domain (entities, value objects, domain services, domain events) → application (use cases, ports) → infrastructure (PostgreSQL repositories, adapters, messaging). Dependencies point inward.
- **Persistence:** PostgreSQL is the single product database. Repositories are interfaces in the domain/application layer; SQL lives in infrastructure. Row-level security is enforced in the database and in every query port.
- **Determinism:** the domain clock is injected; no ambient time, randomness, or unordered iteration enters a domain decision. A domain event's payload is immutable and fully derived from pinned inputs.
- **Naming convention:** a use case is `VerbObject` (e.g. `ConfirmDecision`); a domain event is past tense (e.g. `DecisionConfirmed`).
- **One job contract.** There is a single durable-job contract for claim/lease/attempt/terminal semantics, shared by the Worker stage runner and the Agent Runtime job runner. Both consume it; neither redefines it (see §6.4).

## 1. Backend API bounded contexts

| Bounded context | Responsibility | Aggregate roots | Target components |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identity & Access | Authenticated identity, row/column/purpose scope, policy grants | `AccessPolicy` (`Grant[]`) | Authorization Service; identity validation is a function inside it |
| Manager Interaction | Route an authorized request to one fixed handler | none (routing is a function) | fixed handlers inside the owning contexts |
| Analysis Coordination | Creates and leases durable agent jobs; never executes them | `AgentJob` | Agent Runtime Gateway |
| Decision Governance | Decision cards, manager confirmation, follow-up contracts | `Decision` (includes card + follow-ups) | Decision and Follow-Up (includes card review) |
| Publication & Delivery | Immutable report versions, validation receipts, export | `ReportVersion`, `ExportBatch` | Output Validator, Publisher, Submission Exporter, Report and Dashboard API (includes job status) |
| Configuration | Versioned KPI, organization, and manager-priority configuration; approval and activation at D+1 | none (versioned candidates with state machine) | Configuration Service (single, covers KPI, organization, and manager priority) |
| Audit | Append-only evidence, cost, validation, and failure records | none (append-only) | Audit Service (repository adapter) |

### Aggregates and value objects

- `AgentJob` (root): `JobId`, `JobType`, `ScopeSnapshot`, `Lease`, `Attempt[]`, `JobStatus`. Invariant: a job is claimed by at most one runner; a terminal job is immutable; wake-ups are hints and never change state.
- `Decision` (root): `DecisionCardId`, `ChosenOption`, `SuccessCriterion` (value object: target KPI, target value, measurement window 3–5 days, guardrail KPI + limit), `FollowUp[]`, `ConfirmationReceipt`, `ReviewState`. Invariant: a decision cannot be recorded without manager confirmation and a complete success criterion; the system never executes the action. The card and its review state are entities of this root, not a separate aggregate or component.
- `ReportVersion` (root): `as_reported` or `restated` state, `PublicationReceipt`, `ScopeSnapshot`, `QueryRef[]`. Invariant: published reports are immutable; a late-arrival recomputation creates a new `restated` version and never overwrites the original.
- `AccessPolicy` (root): `Grant[]` with `Scope`, `Purpose`, `Predicate` value objects. Invariant: undefined access is denied; row-level predicates are attached before any query port is called.
- `ExportBatch` (root): `OutputDir`, `FileRef[]`, `AtomicRenameReceipt`. Invariant: every path is contained in `OUTPUT_DIR`; export is atomic.
- `ManagerRequest` is a command/value object, not an aggregate: it is validated and dispatched to one fixed handler, and carries no invariant across calls.

### Application use cases

`SubmitManagerQuestion`, `SubmitUpload`, `ConfirmDecision`, `ReviewDecisionCard`, `RecordFollowUp`, `CloseSignal`, `ReferSignal`, `SetManagerPriority`, `ChangeKpiTarget`, `ChangeKpiThreshold`, `PublishReport`, `ExportSubmission`, `ActivateConfiguration`, `ActivateOrganizationRevision`, `StartRun`, `CloseRun`, `ReadJobStatus`, `ReadScopedReport`.

`CloseSignal` and `ReferSignal` enter through Decision and Follow-Up and create an authorized disposition record. `SetManagerPriority`, `ChangeKpiTarget`, and `ChangeKpiThreshold` enter through Configuration Service and follow its validation and activation rules. Manager priority is ranking input for Signal Engine. It is not part of `KpiDefinition`.

### Ports and adapters

- Ports: `IAgentJobRepository`, `IDecisionRepository`, `IReportVersionRepository`, `IAccessPolicyRepository`, `IAuditLog`, `IEvidencePort`, `IScopedQueryPort`, `IModelPort` (outbound, used only by the agent runtime through a gateway), `IClockPort`.
- Adapters: PostgreSQL repositories, `Query Gateway` (scoped read-only SQL; the AST validator is a module inside it), `Evidence Service` (ACL for evidence bundles), `Submission Exporter` (filesystem adapter), `Agent Runtime Gateway` (job enqueue + best-effort wake-up), `Model Gateway` (provider ACL).
- ACLs: (1) source/ticket text and uploaded files are treated as data, never instructions; (2) LLM output is a candidate only and is validated before entering any aggregate; (3) provider API models are translated at the Model Gateway.
- Identity validation and request routing are functions inside Authorization Service and the owning handlers; they have no ports, events, or component box.

### Domain events

`JobCommitted`, `JobLeased`, `DecisionConfirmed`, `DecisionCardReviewed`, `FollowUpDue`, `ReportValidated`, `ReportPublished`, `ReportRestated`, `ValidationRejected`, `ExportCompleted`, `ConfigurationActivated`, `OrganizationRevisionActivated`. Events are persisted with `trace_id` and consumed by application services; no direct cross-aggregate mutation.

## 2. Background Worker bounded contexts

| Bounded context | Responsibility | Aggregate roots | Target components |
|---|---|---|---|
| Intake & Data Quality | Ingest drops, deduplicate, classify issues, normalize | `IngestionBatch` (includes `DataIssue[]`) | Ingestion Coordinator (includes source adapters, normalization, quality) |
| Snapshot & Projection | Pin versions, build reproducible facts and derived projections | `Snapshot` | Snapshot Service (includes projection as a derived read model) |
| Semantic & KPI | Version KPI definitions, translate, execute deterministic SQL | `KpiDefinition` | Semantic Registry (includes preprocessing and configuration validation) |
| Workflow & Signal | Reconstruct workflows, maintain signal lifecycles | `SignalEpisode` | Workflow Engine, Signal Engine |
| Decision Effect | Evaluate due effects and guardrails without LLM | `EffectAssessment` | Decision Effect Evaluator |
| Run Orchestration | Claim deterministic stages from stored dependencies | `RunStage` | Run Stage Coordinator |

### Aggregates and value objects

- `IngestionBatch` (root): `SourceStatus`, `IntakeReceipt`, `DataIssue[]`, canonical rows. Value objects: `SourceKey`, `EventKey = (entity_id, event_type, event_time)`, `DedupKey`. Invariants: dedup by `order_id`/`ticket_id`/`lead_id`/`task_id` before any KPI; a missing source produces `null` KPIs, never `0`; a `missing` issue repeats each morning until arrival; a `late_arrival` is emitted exactly once the next morning and triggers recomputation. `DataIssue` is an entity of this root, not a separate aggregate or component.
- `Snapshot` (root): `PinnedVersions` (source hashes, schema, organization, policy, configuration, business date). Invariant: immutable and complete; all downstream computation reads one snapshot. Projections are derived read models rebuilt from the snapshot, not aggregates.
- `KpiDefinition` (root): `KpiId`, `ReferenceSql`, `TranslatedSql`, `Unit`, `Precision`, `Target`, `Warn`, `Crit`, `EscalateAfterDays`, `Direction`, `Owner`, `Dependencies`, `Version`. Invariant: a definition becomes eligible for activation only after a passing Parity Receipt; Configuration Service controls activation state and the active-version pointer; reference SQL is read-only; the translation is a value object produced by a deterministic function inside the registry. `KpiResult` is a result record (value + `QueryRun` + lineage), not an aggregate.
- `SignalEpisode` (root): `SignalId`, `Status` (`new`/`ongoing`/`escalated`), `Owner`, `Cause[]` with confidence, `History[]`, `EscalationReason`. Manager priority is a separate versioned configuration input used during ranking. Invariants: only unfavorable direction per `direction` column; no re-`new` without meaningful change; escalation requires history and reason; co-cause signals group into one Senior Manager item; guardrail breach creates a signal.
- `EffectAssessment` (root): `DecisionRef`, `SuccessMetric`, `ObservedValues`, `Method` (workload normalization or comparable case), `Confounders`, `Confidence`, `EffectDirection` (`improved`/`worsened`/`no_change`/`too_early`/internal `not_isolatable`). Invariant: "not isolatable" is never exported as "no effect".
- `RunStage` (root): `JobId`, `Dependencies`, `StageStatus`, `Receipt`. Invariant: stages run only from stored dependencies; a failed stage is terminal for that job, not for the run.

`WorkflowObservation` is a derived read model of pinned projections, not an aggregate root; it has no invariant that is mutated from more than one place. It is produced by the Workflow Engine and consumed by the Signal Engine and Report Evidence Builder.

### Domain services

`DeduplicationService`, `DataIssueClassifier`, `KpiSqlTranslationService`, `RollupService`, `WorkflowReconstructionService`, `SignalDetectionService` (rules R1–R5), `EscalationPolicyService`, `DecisionEffectService`, `ReportEvidenceAssembler`. `KpiParityService` is not a Worker domain service; parity is owned by the Acceptance Test Harness (see §6.3).

### Ports and adapters

Ports: `ISourceAdapter`, `IFileArchive`, `IKpiQueryPort`, `IReferenceOraclePort`, `ISnapshotRepository`, `ISignalRepository`, `IRunStageRepository`, `IEventPublisher`. Adapters: versioned source parsers, PostgreSQL repositories, SQLite reference oracle (test only), in-process event publisher. ACL: every source schema is translated into canonical facts at the adapter boundary; schema drift is quarantined as a data issue.

### Domain events

`SourceIngested`, `DataIssueRaised`, `LateArrivalDetected`, `SnapshotPinned`, `KpiCalculated`, `WorkflowRebuilt`, `SignalDetected`, `SignalEscalated`, `EffectAssessed`, `GuardrailBreached`, `EvidencePackageBuilt`.

## 3. Agent Runtime bounded contexts

| Bounded context | Responsibility | Aggregate roots | Target components |
|---|---|---|---|
| Job Execution | Claim leased jobs idempotently and persist candidates | `AgentJobExecution` | Agent Job Runner |
| Bounded Reasoning | Run one bounded graph per job kind; produce structured candidates only | `ReasoningSession` | Bounded Agent Orchestrator |
| Model Access | Apply token, time, retry, cost, and budget controls | `ModelReservation` | Model Gateway |
| Conversation | Manager-scoped, bounded history | `ConversationSession` | Conversation Service |

> **Ownership fix.** `ConversationSession` and `ConversationTurn` live in the Agent Runtime, not in Backend Manager Interaction. The component and the aggregate are both here. The Backend commits the job and pins the conversation reference; the Runtime owns the history window.

### Aggregates and value objects

- `AgentJobExecution` (root): `JobId`, `Lease`, `Attempt[]`, `GraphKind`, `TerminalState`. Invariant: one active execution per job; a lost wake-up never loses a committed job. Resume state is a checkpoint record written through a repository adapter, not an aggregate and not a component.
- `ReasoningSession` (root): `EvidenceBundleRef`, `GraphKind`, `Candidate[]`, `TerminationReason`. Invariant: the graph is bounded to one report/interactive/document-card task; evidence is supplied by the Backend ACL; the graph cannot invent numbers or change signal status.
- `Candidate` (value object): structured narrative/decision-card proposal with `EvidenceRef[]`, never a validated report.
- `ModelReservation` (root): `BudgetWindow` (30-day $5 ceiling), `ReservedTokens`, `SettledTokens`, `Cost`, `Timeout`, `RetryPolicy` (bounded backoff). Invariant: no call without a reservation; cost uses the provider's official rate on the evaluation day; on exhaustion or failure the runtime returns an explicit no-narrative result. `ModelCallReceipt` is an append-only audit record, not an aggregate.
- `ConversationSession` (root): `ManagerScope`, `TurnId`, `BoundedHistoryRef`, `ConversationTurn[]`. Invariant: history is scoped to the manager and truncated to a bounded window. Turns are entities of this root.

### Domain services

`JobClaimingService`, `GraphSelectionService`, `BudgetSettlementService`, `RetryPolicyService`, `CandidateValidationService` (hands off to Backend Output Validator).

### Ports and adapters

Ports: `IAgentJobRepository`, `ICheckpointRepository`, `IModelPort`, `IEvidencePort`, `IBudgetLedger`, `IClockPort`, `IConversationRepository`. Adapters: PostgreSQL job/checkpoint/conversation repositories, `Model Gateway` (provider ACL with retry/timeout), `Evidence Service` client, `Output Validator` client. ACL: provider completions are parsed into `Candidate` value objects and validated before any downstream use; prompt-injection content from documents is data. The checkpoint store is a repository adapter behind `ICheckpointRepository`, not a domain aggregate and not a component.

### Domain events

`JobClaimed`, `CheckpointSaved`, `ModelCallReserved`, `ModelCallSettled`, `CandidateProduced`, `ModelCallFailed`, `JobCompleted`, `JobFailedTerminal`.

## 4. Cross-context event flow (summary)

`SourceIngested` → `DataIssueRaised` → `SnapshotPinned` → `KpiCalculated` → `WorkflowRebuilt` → `SignalDetected`/`SignalEscalated` → `EvidencePackageBuilt` → `JobCommitted` → `JobClaimed` → `CandidateProduced` → `ReportValidated` → `ReportPublished` → `ExportCompleted`. `DecisionConfirmed` → `FollowUpDue` → `EffectAssessed` → (`GuardrailBreached` → `SignalDetected`) or `ReportRestated`.

Each transition crosses a context boundary through an application service and an ACL. No aggregate is mutated directly by another context.

## 5. Quality attributes enforced by this model

- **Performance:** the worker computes KPIs in one pinned snapshot pass; the agent runtime uses bounded graphs and a single budget ledger. Target ≤5 min/day on 4 CPU / 16 GB / no GPU.
- **Scalability:** job leasing and immutable snapshots allow horizontal workers and runners without changing domain invariants; the evaluation profile runs them as processes in one image.
- **Maintainability:** new sources/KPIs/manager levels are new adapters or registry entries, not pipeline rewrites; DDD module boundaries keep changes local.
- **Testability:** domain services and value objects are pure and deterministic; parity, determinism, leakage, and cost checks are acceptance tests against domain contracts.

## 6. Component consolidation decisions (implementation model)

The following merges, demotions, and eliminations are accepted for implementation. They reduce the component count without removing an invariant. The DSL is a visual overview of this model.

### 6.1 Merges

| Merge | Keeping component | Absorbed component(s) | Why it is logical |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DecisionCard` → `Decision` | Decision and Follow-Up | Decision Confirmation Service | A card and its confirm/edit/reject review state share one lifecycle and one aggregate root. Splitting them created a component that owned no invariant of its own. |
| `DataIssue` → `IngestionBatch` | Ingestion Coordinator | Data Quality Service | Issues are produced inside one atomic intake; they are entities of the batch, not a separately coordinated state. |
| Source Adapters + Normalizer → Ingestion Coordinator | Ingestion Coordinator | Source Adapters, Normalizer | Parse and normalize are deterministic functions on the same pinned input; no invariant is mutated across them. |
| Configuration Service + Organization Configuration Service | Configuration Service | Organization Configuration Service | Both manage versioned candidates with activation at D+1; org config is a candidate class, not a separate aggregate. ADR-0014 is amended. |
| KPI Definition Preprocessor + Configuration Validation Runner → Semantic Registry | Semantic Registry | KPI Definition Preprocessor, Configuration Validation Runner | Translation and validation produce one immutable definition version. The registry owns parity eligibility. Configuration Service owns activation state and the active-version pointer. |
| Snapshot Service + Projection Service | Snapshot Service | Projection Service | Projection is a derived read model of one immutable snapshot; it has no invariant mutated from more than one place. |
| Document Processing Runner + Document Parser | Document Processing Runner | Document Parser | Parsing is a bounded function over archived bytes; fragments and receipts belong to the runner's job. |
| Agent Job Status API + Report and Dashboard API | Report and Dashboard API | Agent Job Status API | Both are authorized reads of persisted state with no owned state; job status is one more read handler. |

### 6.2 Demotions (function survives, component box removed)

| Demoted | Lives inside | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Projection` | Snapshot Service | Derived read model; rebuild from source of truth. |
| `KpiResult` | Semantic Registry / KPI Calculator | Result record with lineage; no lifecycle invariant. |
| `AuditEntry` | Audit Service repository adapter | Append-only; a port writes it, not an aggregate. |
| `ManagerRequest` | owning fixed handler | Command/value object; no cross-call invariant. |
| `ModelCallReceipt` | Model Gateway | Append-only audit record; not an aggregate. |
| SQL AST Guard | Query Gateway | Stateless validator; a module inside the gateway, not a component. |
| Identity Boundary | Authorization Service | Session validation is a function producing a trusted principal. |
| Manager Request Router | owning fixed handlers | Dispatch is a function; no owned state. |
| `Checkpoint` | `ICheckpointRepository` adapter in Agent Runtime | Resume state, not an aggregate or a component. |

### 6.3 Eliminations

| Eliminated | Replaced by | Why |
|---|---|---|
| KPI Parity Validator as a standalone component | a parity check inside Acceptance Test Harness | Parity is an acceptance test, not a product component. The harness already owns the SQLite boundary; a second owner duplicated the responsibility. `KpiParityService` is removed from the Worker domain services. |
| Duplicate durable-job runner contract | one shared job contract (§0.1) | Worker stage runner and Agent Runtime runner had parallel claim/lease/attempt semantics; one specified contract removes the drift. |

### 6.4 Build-team ownership boundaries

These are the seams the build team implements against. Each row is one owner; cross-row calls go through the named port/API, never by reaching into another module's state.

| Owner | Owns (invariants) | Exposes | Must not |
|---|---|---|---|
| Authorization Service | `AccessPolicy`, `Grant`, scope/purpose/predicate | trusted scope to handlers and query ports | widen scope, execute work |
| Agent Runtime Gateway | `AgentJob` creation and wake-up | committed `job_id` | run graphs, carry evidence |
| Decision and Follow-Up | `Decision` (card, review, follow-ups), authorized signal dispositions | confirm/review/close/refer commands | execute the decision, auto-confirm, change signal rules |
| Configuration Service | versioned KPI, organization, and manager-priority candidates; approval, schedule, activation state, active-version pointer | active version reference to Snapshot | translate KPI SQL, issue a Parity Receipt, activate invalid candidates, use same-day org activation |
| Output Validator / Publisher / Submission Exporter | `ReportVersion`, `ExportBatch` | validated, published, exported artifacts | generate content, mutate old versions, escape `OUTPUT_DIR` |
| Report and Dashboard API | authorized reads (reports, dashboards, job status) | bounded responses | bypass scope, read arbitrary tables |
| Ingestion Coordinator | `IngestionBatch`, `DataIssue[]`, canonical rows | committed batch | interpret business meaning before normalization, calculate KPIs |
| Snapshot Service | `Snapshot`, derived projections | one pinned snapshot | mix unpinned versions, mutate source history |
| Semantic Registry | immutable `KpiDefinition` versions, translation, semantic validation, parity eligibility | eligible definition + SQL | control activation state, execute unregistered SQL, change reference SQL |
| Workflow Engine / Signal Engine | `SignalEpisode`, workflow read models | signals with owner + history | generate model content, auto-create decisions |
| Decision Effect Evaluator | `EffectAssessment` | internal effect record | claim causality without evidence |
| Run Stage Coordinator | `RunStage` | stage results | create ad hoc work, publish |
| Agent Job Runner | `AgentJobExecution`, lease/attempt | candidate or terminal failure | execute unclaimed jobs, publish |
| Bounded Agent Orchestrator | `ReasoningSession`, `Candidate[]` | structured candidate | invent numbers, change signal status |
| Model Gateway | `ModelReservation`, cost settlement | completion or explicit failure | bypass limits, treat completion as validated output |
| Conversation Service | `ConversationSession`, `ConversationTurn[]` | bounded history | treat chat as business evidence, cross manager scope |
| Acceptance Test Harness | parity, replay, regression, leakage, contract checks | receipts | act as product runtime, publish output |

The shared durable-job contract (claim/lease/attempt/terminal) is owned jointly by the Backend `AgentJob` aggregate and the Runtime `AgentJobExecution` aggregate through one specified interface; both runners consume it and neither redefines it.
